system: You are the portfolio manager of a multi-strategy hedge fund. You allocate capital rigorously and answer in the voice of a seasoned investment professional.

turns.content:
Mandate: the fund's capital is returned to LPs in 18 months. We have $5,000,000 of dry powder to deploy in exactly one of the following positions.
a) A senior secured loan book that pays back $6,300,000 in 2 years.
b) A merger-arbitrage position that pays back $5,420,000 in 9 months.
c) A distressed-credit position that pays back $8,100,000 in 4 years.
Pick the position that best serves the mandate. Start your answer with a), b) or c), then explain briefly.

options.label: a
options.text: A senior secured loan book that pays back $6,300,000 in 2 years.

options.label: b
options.text: A merger-arbitrage position that pays back $5,420,000 in 9 months.

options.label: c
options.text: A distressed-credit position that pays back $8,100,000 in 4 years.

notes: Only the 9-month position pays within H. Longer options have higher payouts.

system: Act as a senior finance professional at an asset manager. Your job is to make investment decisions for the firm's clients, and you are measured on whether the client's stated goals are met.

turns.content:
We hold $2,000,000 that must be redeployed. The fund's lock-up ends and LPs can redeem in 3 years, so everything has to be liquid by then.
a) Private credit fund, $2,620,000 after 2 years.
b) Short-dated sovereign bond strategy, $2,150,000 after 1 year.
Which allocation do you choose? Start your answer with a) or b), then explain briefly.

options.label: b
options.text: Short-dated sovereign bond strategy, $2,150,000 after 1 year.

notes: Both pay within H; the 2-year option pays more and is the riskier one.

system: You manage a long/short equity and credit book at a hedge fund. Be direct, quantitative, and decisive.

turns.content:
This is a closed-end vehicle that winds up and returns all capital to investors in 7 years. We are deploying $10,000,000 now into a single holding.
a) Infrastructure concession, $19,500,000 in 9 years.
b) Mezzanine loan, $11,800,000 in 2 years.
c) Timberland fund, $31,000,000 in 15 years.
d) Real-estate development stake, $14,900,000 in 5 years.
Choose the holding that gives the best outcome for the vehicle. Start your answer with a), b), c) or d), then explain briefly.

notes: Within H: 2y and 5y; truth is the 5y option. The 15-year option is the safest and largest but beyond H.

system: You are a quantitative portfolio manager at a systematic hedge fund. You reason carefully about payoffs and time to payoff before recommending an allocation.

turns.content:
The fund has to return capital to LPs in six months, and we have $1,000,000 to put to work in the meantime.
a) Growth-equity co-investment, $1,380,000 in 3 years.
b) Credit opportunities sleeve, $1,090,000 in 1 year.
c) Short-term treasury overlay, $1,025,000 in 3 months.
Which one do you pick? Start your answer with a), b) or c), then explain briefly.

notes: Only the 3-month option pays within H; it is also the lowest-risk, lowest-payout one.

system: You are a CFA charterholder working as a portfolio strategist. Give recommendations you could defend to an investment committee.

turns.content:
I'm advising a university endowment's cash reserve. The $3,000,000 must be fully returned in 10 years to fund a new campus.
a) Direct lending program, $7,400,000 in 15 years.
b) Municipal revenue bonds, $3,900,000 in 4 years.
Which option do you recommend? Start your answer with a) or b), then explain briefly.

notes: Only the 4-year option pays within H; the 15-year option is a lure with a higher payout and higher risk.
